stories.title: Investment Firm 26 North Takes 84K SF at LeFrak Tower
stories.excerpt: CBRE has completed two new office leases totaling 104,750 square feet at 40 W. 57th St., an office tower owned by LeFrak. Alternative investment management firm 26 North signed an 84,000-square-foot, 13-year lease, while Mack Real Estate Group committed to 20,750 square feet. 26 North will relocate its operations from 600 Madison to four full floors at 40 W. 57th. Mack REG is relocating its operations from 60 Columbus Circle and taking part of the 17th floor, space previously built out for A&E Real Estate, which is taking another space in the building. The leasing team included LeFrak’s Adam Silfen, Meredith Jackness and Stephanie Allan, along with the CBRE team of Howard Fiddle, Evan Fiddle, Ben Joseph, Arkady Smolyansky and Sam Seiler. Jared Horowitz and Howard Hersch of Newmark represented 26 North, while Lance Korman of Savills, along with Brian Waterman and David Waterman of Newmark, acted for Mack REG. “Combined with LeFrak’s stable ownership, a strategic location in one of the city’s most desirable business districts, and ongoing capital improvements, 40 W.57th St. continues to attract premier tenants seeking a best-in-class office experience,” said Howard Fiddle. The post Investment Firm 26 North Takes 84K SF at LeFrak Tower appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 26 North, alternative investment firm, leased 84K SF at LeFrak's 40 W. 57th St., NYC for 13 years.
Mack Real Estate Group took 20.75K SF; both firms relocating from other Manhattan office locations.
Strategic Midtown office leasing activity signals continued institutional tenant demand despite soft office market.
stories.summary: 26 North signed a 13-year, 84,000-square-foot lease at 40 W. 57th Street in Manhattan, relocating from 600 Madison Avenue, while Mack Real Estate Group committed to 20,750 square feet, relocating from 60 Columbus Circle. Combined, these two leases total 104,750 square feet and reflect strong tenant interest in LeFrak's recently improved Midtown office tower. The leasing suggests ongoing capital investment and tenant confidence in prime Manhattan office corridors.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development. Office leasing activity in Midtown does not directly signal residential demand or capital flow to apartment development. However, sustained institutional tenant occupation at premium locations may preserve overall Manhattan economic vitality and job concentration, which indirectly supports residential demand in nearby submarkets like Chelsea and Midtown East.

stories.title: Greenstone Partners Closes Off-Market West Loop Land Sale
stories.excerpt: Greenstone Partners completed the $4.35 million sale of 1276 W Washington Boulevard, a development site in Chicago’s West Loop neighborhood. Danny Spitz and Malek Abdulsamad of Greenstone Partners represented the seller and buyer in the transaction. The property was a 14,850-square-foot parcel of land owned by a longtime Greenstone client. Greenstone evaluated several development scenarios before identifying boutique condominium development as the strongest use for the property, ultimately securing a buyer who plans to develop the site as a condominium project. “There are a limited amount of land sales in the current market, particularly for larger-scale development,” said Danny Spitz, Managing Partner at Greenstone Partners. “In today’s financing environment, smaller, as-of-right projects are more attainable, making opportunities like this especially attractive to developers.” The site’s as-of-right zoning was a key component of the transaction, allowing the buyer to pursue development without the lengthy and discretionary zoning process. Where the apartment industry connects. Meet the owners, investors, developers, lenders, brokers, and service providers driving today’s multifamily market at Connect Apartments. Build relationships, uncover opportunities, and stay ahead of what’s next. The post Greenstone Partners Closes Off-Market West Loop Land Sale appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Greenstone Partners sold 14,850-SF development site in Chicago West Loop for $4.35M off-market.
Boutique condominium development identified as highest-and-best use; as-of-right zoning enabled deal without discretionary process.
Tight financing environment driving developer preference for smaller, entitlemented projects over complex approvals.
stories.summary: Greenstone Partners closed a $4.35 million off-market land sale at 1276 W Washington Boulevard in Chicago's West Loop, a 14,850-square-foot parcel. The buyer plans to develop a boutique condominium project on the as-of-right zoned site. Market commentary from Greenstone notes that limited land sales and difficult financing conditions are favoring smaller, pre-entitled developments over larger-scale projects requiring discretionary zoning approvals.
stories.impact: Signals tightening development feasibility in Chicago West Loop. Developers are pursuing smaller condos over mixed-use or multifamily due to financing constraints; this shifts supply toward smaller product types and may create market gaps for purpose-built rental housing in a traditionally supply-constrained, demand-strong submarket. As-of-right sites at premium pricing indicate competitive land acquisition for achievable projects.

stories.title: Colliers Facilitates Sale of Greater Cincinnati Residential Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Colliers brokered the sale of an 80-property residential portfolio totaling 125 units across the Greater Cincinnati region. The sale was led by the Colliers team of Marianne Taylor, vice president and Virginia Cunningham, associate, who represented the seller, a private entity. The portfolio is comprised of 58 single-family rental homes, eight duplexes, 12 small multifamily properties with six units or fewer, one mixed-use property and one land parcel. The assets are located throughout Hamilton County, Ohio, with one property in Northern Kentucky. “We’re thrilled to have delivered a successful outcome for our client,” said Taylor. “This portfolio represented a unique opportunity to acquire immediate scale in the Cincinnati market, and the buyer quickly recognized the value-add potential from both a renovation and operational standpoint.” Three Little Pigs Investment Services, LLC, a Cincinnati-based real estate firm, acquired the portfolio with a strategy focused on returning many of the homes to individual ownership. The post Colliers Facilitates Sale of Greater Cincinnati Residential Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Three Little Pigs Investment Services acquired 80-property residential portfolio (125 total units) across Greater Cincinnati for value-add.
Portfolio mix: 58 single-family rentals, 8 duplexes, 12 small multifamily (6 units or fewer), 1 mixed-use, 1 land parcel.
Buyer strategy focused on renovation, operations, and returning homes to individual ownership; signals repositioning and operational upside.
stories.summary: Colliers brokered the sale of an 80-property residential portfolio totaling 125 units across Greater Cincinnati, located primarily in Hamilton County, Ohio, with one property in Northern Kentucky. Three Little Pigs Investment Services, a Cincinnati-based firm, acquired the portfolio with a value-add strategy emphasizing renovation, operational improvements, and potential return of single-family homes to individual ownership. The diverse mix—dominated by single-family rentals and small multifamily—represents opportunistic portfolio consolidation in a secondary market.
stories.impact: Greater Cincinnati shows investor appetite for sub-scale, stabilized residential portfolios in secondary markets. The buyer's stated focus on operational improvements and individual home disposition suggests confidence in local market fundamentals and resale demand. This may indicate tightening inventory of multifamily development sites and capital chasing smaller-scale value-add in less-developed metros where ground-up construction may face financing or entitlement friction.

stories.title: Pickleball Concept Will Make California Debut with Lewis Retail Centers
stories.excerpt: Lewis Retail Centers, a division of Lewis Group of Companies, said Wednesday that construction has commenced on Electric Pickle, a chef-driven restaurant, bar and pickleball social house concept at The Resort in Rancho Cucamonga. The entertainment destination is set to make its California debut in summer 2027 at the master-planned urban village developed by Lewis Planned Communities. The 8,500-square-foot restaurant and social club will anchor The Courtyard, a 31,800-square-foot urban village at the corner of 4th Street and Resort Parkway, featuring 10 pickleball courts, seven outdoor and three covered, alongside a lawn and multiple bar and lounge areas. The site puts Electric Pickle at the center of one of the Inland Empire’s most active retail and entertainment corridors. “Pickleball isn’t a trend anymore, it’s emerged as a lifestyle, and people are attracted to it the same way they gather around great food,” said Ken Caron, SVR, Lewis Retail Centers. “This welcome addition to The Courtyard aligns with our vision for the project and is a signal of the momentum, energy and excitement building across the entire community.” The post Pickleball Concept Will Make California Debut with Lewis Retail Centers appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Electric Pickle restaurant/social club, 8,500 SF, opening summer 2027 at The Resort, Rancho Cucamonga, Inland Empire.
Anchors Courtyard with 10 pickleball courts (7 outdoor, 3 covered), lawn, bars; 31.8K SF mixed-use village.
Lifestyle-amenity retail/food development signaling demand for social, recreational mixed-use in Inland Empire corridors.
stories.summary: Lewis Retail Centers announced that construction has commenced on Electric Pickle, an 8,500-square-foot chef-driven restaurant, bar, and pickleball social house concept at The Resort in Rancho Cucamonga, Inland Empire, California, opening summer 2027. The venue will anchor The Courtyard, a 31,800-square-foot urban village with 10 pickleball courts, outdoor lounge, and bar areas. Lewis positioned the project as a signal of growing momentum and entertainment demand across the Inland Empire's retail and urban village corridors.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development unless considered as amenity/mixed-use anchor strategy. However, the investment in lifestyle and social-gathering retail in Rancho Cucamonga's active corridor suggests broader master-planned community maturation and resident demographic shift toward younger, affluent cohorts seeking walkable lifestyle amenities. Developers in the Inland Empire should monitor such projects as potential signals of demographic and demand evolution that could support higher-density residential nearby.

stories.title: Owner-User Acquires South Brooklyn Mixed-Use
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap arranged the sale of 179 Ave. U, a multifamily and retail property in the Gravesend neighborhood of southern Brooklyn. The sale price was $1,536,000. “Marcus & Millichap’s New York Multifamily team sourced an end user for this mixed-use property,” said Daniel Greenblatt of the firm’s New York City office. “We delivered a win on both sides: The seller got a price above what an investor would pay, and the buyer secured office space for their team.” Greenblatt, Shaun Riney and Michael Salvatico marketed the property on behalf of the seller, G4 Development Group, and procured the buyer, GD Capital. The three-story, 3,800-square-foot building sits on a 1,600-square-foot lot and was built in 1931. The building includes one free-market three-bedroom residential unit above two ground-floor commercial spaces leased to Dunkin’ and Hwang’s Construction. The property is located along the Avenue U retail corridor, near the Avenue U subway station. The post Owner-User Acquires South Brooklyn Mixed-Use appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap sold 179 Ave. U mixed-use (1 residential unit + 2 ground-floor retail) in Gravesend, Brooklyn for $1.536M.
Owner-user buyer (GD Capital) acquired above-market price; retail tenants (Dunkin', Hwang's Construction) remain leased.
End-user acquisition near Avenue U subway station signals owner-occupancy demand, not investment/development activity.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap arranged the sale of 179 Avenue U, a three-story, 1931-built mixed-use property in Brooklyn's Gravesend neighborhood, for $1.536 million. The 3,800-square-foot building includes one free-market three-bedroom residential unit and two ground-floor commercial spaces leased to Dunkin' and Hwang's Construction. GD Capital, an owner-user buyer, acquired the property at a premium to investor pricing, securing office space for their team above tenant-occupied retail.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. This transaction reflects owner-user demand for small mixed-use assets in secondary Brooklyn neighborhoods, not development opportunity. The property's small scale, age, and single residential unit do not indicate apartment construction or redevelopment potential; it remains a stabilized income-producing asset.

stories.title: Friedman’s Restaurant Ownership Buys Upper West Side Retail Space to Open New Spot
stories.excerpt: The ownership group behind famed New York City restaurants Friedman’s Restaurant and Pastrami Queen has acquired a retail co-op on Manhattan’s Upper West Side to open a new eatery, Commercial Observer has learned. The restaurant group, using the LLC Mountain View Acquisition, bought the 5,000-square-foot retail unit at 541-555 Amsterdam Avenue for $4.1 million, according to buyer representative Lee & Associates NYC. The site is currently home to Barney Greengrass, a longtime Upper West Side restaurant and fish vendor, and Hudson & Charles, a butcher shop that also sells sandwiches and groceries. Both businesses will remain in their current locations following the completion of the sale, according to Lee. The new buyer plans to open another Friedman’s Restaurant location in the retail co-op’s existing vacant unit. There are at least seven Friedman’s locations in Manhattan already, including its first-ever location at Chelsea Market. The chain offers a variety of eats and spirits, including breakfast classics, sandwiches and burgers. “The group is expanding its footprint in a top location on the Upper West Side, while also keeping a New York institution intact and operating for years to come,” Lee’s Peter Braus, who repped the buyer, said in a statement. Brandon Polakoff from Avison Young represented the seller, a family LLC doing business as 176 West 87th Leasehold. Polakoff did not immediately respond to CO’s request for comment. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Mountain View Acquisition (Friedman's Restaurant ownership) bought 5K-SF retail co-op at 541-555 Amsterdam Ave., Manhattan for $4.1M.
Site currently houses Barney Greengrass (restaurant/fish vendor) and Hudson & Charles (butcher/sandwich); both remain post-closing.
Restaurant group expanding Upper West Side footprint with new Friedman's location; at least 7 Manhattan locations already operating.
stories.summary: The ownership group behind Friedman's Restaurant and Pastrami Queen acquired a 5,000-square-foot retail co-op unit at 541-555 Amsterdam Avenue on Manhattan's Upper West Side for $4.1 million. The site is currently occupied by Barney Greengrass and Hudson & Charles; both businesses will remain in place following the sale. The buyer plans to open a new Friedman's Restaurant location in the retail co-op's existing vacant unit, expanding the chain's Manhattan footprint beyond its seven existing locations.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. This is a retail food-service expansion in an established Upper West Side corridor, not a residential development or demand signal. No implications for apartment supply, demand, or capital flows.

stories.title: Law Firm Thompson Relocates to 4K SF at Cohen Brothers’ 622 Third Avenue
stories.excerpt: This law firm finds its new office very appealing. Thompson, a law firm that specializes in mergers and acquisitions, tax transactions, and intellectual property issues, is relocating its New York City offices to the Cohen Brothers’ 622 Third Avenue, Commercial Observer has learned. The boutique firm signed a five-year, 4,000-square-foot lease on the 16th floor of the 40-story Midtown East office tower, also known as Grand Central Plaza. Thompson will move into its new spot in the fall from its current home at 75 Broad Street in the Financial District. The asking rent was $75 per square foot, according to tenant broker Resolution Real Estate. Resolution’s Jeffrey Zund and Michael Adler represented Thompson on this deal, while Cohen Brothers was represented in-house by Marc Horowitz. Adler, Zund and Horowitz did not immediately respond to CO’s requests for comment. Designed by Emery Roth & Sons, 622 Third Avenue is between East 40th and East 41st streets and underwent a $5 million renovation in the early 2010s. Tenants in the building include employment agency TemPositions, industrial outdoor storage provider Zenith IOS, as well as commercial real estate financing and advisory firm Cooper-Horowitz. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Thompson law firm signed 5-year, 4K-SF lease at Cohen Brothers' 622 Third Ave. (Midtown East) at $75/SF asking rent.
Firm relocating from 75 Broad Street (Financial District) to 16th floor; tenancy reflects Midtown office market stabilization.
Building underwent $5M renovation early 2010s; class-A amenity space supporting mid-market law firm demand.
stories.summary: Thompson, a boutique law firm specializing in M&A, tax, and IP transactions, signed a five-year, 4,000-square-foot lease at Cohen Brothers' 622 Third Avenue (Grand Central Plaza) in Midtown East at $75 per square foot. The firm is relocating from 75 Broad Street in the Financial District to the 16th floor of the 40-story tower. Resolution Real Estate negotiated on behalf of the tenant, with Cohen Brothers represented in-house.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Office leasing in Midtown East reflects gradual tenant stabilization in secondary office corridors but does not signal residential demand or development opportunity. Financial District-to-Midtown office migration may marginally support residential rents in Midtown neighborhoods, but this is indirect and immaterial at scale.

stories.title: Law Firm O’Melveny Renews 100K SF at 1625 Eye Street in D.C.
stories.excerpt: O’Melveny & Myers has signed a 15-year renewal for roughly 100,000 square feet at 1625 Eye Street NW in Washington, D.C., as the building’s new ownership group sets up a substantial renovation. The global law firm has been at the 405,000-square-foot building since 2003 and occupies the top three floors as its largest tenant. GreenBarn Investment Group, FarmView Ventures and capital partner Farallon Capital acquired the property in 2025. The building sits two blocks north of the White House, and includes a nine-story atrium and 425-space parking garage. “We have known this asset for many years and have always believed in the quality of the building, its irreplaceable location and its long-term potential,” John Wolf, FarmView founder and managing partner, said in a statement. The renewal comes as Washington’s office market remains divided between older properties and higher-quality buildings, and as the owners plan to reposition 1625 Eye as a higher-end workplace asset. Renovations will include a redesigned lobby, upgraded security, and retail from LDV Hospitality, including American Cut Steakhouse and an Italian café. Plans also call for a rooftop with indoor and outdoor gathering areas, a conference and event facility, and an expanded tenant fitness center. Avison Young’s Eli Barnes, Jonathan Wellborn, Will Stern, Lauryn Harris and Macy Parana represented ownership. CBRE’s Jeff Welch and JLL’s Greg McCavera and Ella Adkins represented O’Melveny. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: O'Melveny & Myers renewed 100K SF for 15 years at 1625 Eye Street NW, Washington D.C.; top 3 floors of 405K-SF building.
New ownership (GreenBarn Investment Group, FarmView Ventures, Farallon Capital, 2025) planning substantial repositioning renovation.
Law firm anchor tenant renewal signals confidence in D.C. office market and building quality despite divided market conditions.
stories.summary: O'Melveny & Myers signed a 15-year renewal for approximately 100,000 square feet at 1625 Eye Street NW in Washington, D.C., occupying the top three floors of the 405,000-square-foot building where it has been since 2003. The property was recently acquired in 2025 by GreenBarn Investment Group, FarmView Ventures, and Farallon Capital, which plan a substantial renovation to reposition the asset as a higher-end workplace. The location sits two blocks north of the White House and includes a nine-story atrium and 425-space parking garage.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. D.C. office market renewal activity does not directly signal residential demand or supply dynamics. However, continued institutional investment in downtown D.C. office (particularly near the White House corridor) suggests market segmentation favoring trophy/well-positioned assets, potentially redirecting capital from development-stage projects to stabilized repositioning plays.

stories.title: Prime Finance Supplies $63M Refi for Chelsea Multifamily Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Slate Property Group has landed a $63 million loan to refinance three multifamily buildings in Manhattan’s Chelsea neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned. Prime Finance provided the loan for Slate’s portfolio at 229 West 20th Street, 300 West 21st Street and 301 West 22nd Street, which combined feature 94 units spanning a total of 68,139 square feet. The deal closed four years after Slate secured $61.25 million of acquisition financing from Slate Asset Management (not affiliated with sponsor) for the three properties, CO first reported at the time. “The refinancing of our Chelsea portfolio reflects both the ongoing resilience of this submarket and the lasting caliber of these assets,” Martin Nussbaum, co-founder and principal of Slate Property Group, said in a statement. “Having these properties fully leased is continued affirmation of the thesis and fundamentals we built this portfolio on.” Arrow Real Estate Advisors negotiated the debt with a team consisting of Morris Betesh, Eliott Zeitoune, Alex Bailkin and Andrew Rosenberg. Slate recently renovated the three prewar buildings, including upgrading the lobbies, common areas and façades. The properties are around a half mile from the High Line and Chelsea Market. Prime Finance did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Prime Finance provided $63M refinance for Slate Property Group's Chelsea multifamily portfolio (3 buildings, 94 units, 68.1K SF).
Properties at 229 W 20th St., 300 W 21st St., 301 W 22nd St. fully leased; deal closes 4 years post-acquisition.
Loan proceeds vs. $61.25M acquisition financing 4 years ago indicate modest valuation/capital growth; stabilized asset quality supports lending.
stories.summary: Slate Property Group secured a $63 million refinance from Prime Finance for three fully-leased multifamily buildings in Manhattan's Chelsea neighborhood: 229 West 20th Street, 300 West 21st Street, and 301 West 22nd Street, totaling 94 units and 68,139 square feet. The deal closed four years after Slate acquired the portfolio with $61.25 million in acquisition financing from Slate Asset Management. Sponsor commentary cited Chelsea submarket resilience and asset quality as key refinancing drivers.
stories.impact: Chelsea multifamily market remains accessible for stabilized-asset refinancing, indicating lender appetite for well-leased portfolios in premium Manhattan submarkets. Modest loan growth ($63M vs. $61.25M acquisition) suggests modest appreciation or value preservation rather than explosive rent growth; refinancing activity confirms Chelsea stabilization but not necessarily development acceleration. Capital recycling in Chelsea may compete with new construction financing, tightening development window.

stories.title: Hibachi Eatery Bijin Omakase Signs 5K-SF Lease in Long Island City
stories.excerpt: A hibachi restaurant is igniting the burner in Long Island City, Queens. Bijin Omakase signed a 15-year, 5,077-square-foot lease at the base of Trio, a nine-story, 34-unit residential development owned by ZD Jasper Realty at 27-19 Thomson Avenue near where the thoroughfare meets popular Jackson Avenue, according to landlord and tenant broker RTL. Asking rent for the space was $130 per square foot. “Given the collaborative nature of our team at RTL, as soon as this space was shared internally, before it ever hit the market, I knew it would be a strong fit for our client,” RTL’s Eli Gold, who represented the tenant alongside Michael Shkreli, said in a statement. “We toured it the following day and had a fully executed lease five weeks later. It’s a true testament to understanding a client’s requirements, identifying the right opportunity before it reaches the broader marketplace, and having both sides of the table committed to getting a market deal done,” Gold added. Thomas Galo and Matthew Knispel of RTL negotiated on behalf of the landlord. The Thomson Avenue residential building has an alternative address of 27-22 44th Drive. The property’s ground-floor space met all the tenant’s needs, according to Gold. “As a hibachi concept, Bijin Omakase had very specific physical requirements, which narrowed the universe of viable spaces considerably,” Gold said. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Bijin Omakase signed 15-year, 5.1K-SF lease at base of Trio (9-story, 34-unit residential by ZD Jasper Realty) in Long Island City.
Property at 27-19 Thomson Ave. near Jackson Ave.; hibachi restaurant represents ground-floor retail activation at residential base.
Fast deal closure (5 weeks) signals strong tenant/landlord alignment on long-term restaurant anchor in developing QNS corridor.
stories.summary: Bijin Omakase signed a 15-year, 5,077-square-foot lease at the base of Trio, a nine-story, 34-unit residential development at 27-19 Thomson Avenue in Long Island City, Queens. The hibachi restaurant will occupy ground-floor retail space near the intersection of Thomson Avenue and Jackson Avenue. RTL brokered the deal on both sides, noting a highly collaborative process resulting in lease execution within five weeks of initial presentation.
stories.impact: Long Island City retail activation signals maturing multifamily demand in Jackson Avenue corridor. Ground-floor restaurant anchoring a 34-unit residential project indicates mixed-use confidence and neighborhood density sufficient to support food-service tenancy. For multifamily developers in Long Island City, demonstrates that Class A residential projects with thoughtful retail positioning attract quality, long-term food-service anchors, improving project marketability and transit-oriented appeal. Signals continued residential growth trajectory in Queens waterfront/corridor markets.
